title: Independence of the K-flat model
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, $T$ a scheme, and let
$\mathcal P^\bullet\to\mathcal Q^\bullet$ be a quasi-isomorphism of
K-flat complexes of
$\Lambda_T$-module sheaves. Then for every complex
$\mathcal F^\bullet$ of $\Lambda_T$-module sheaves the induced map

$$
\mathcal F^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal P^\bullet
\longrightarrow
\mathcal F^\bullet\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal Q^\bullet
$$

is a quasi-isomorphism; consequently
$K_1\kunotimes{\Lambda}K_2$ of [def-kun-derived-tensor] is
independent, up to canonical isomorphism in $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, of
the chosen K-flat model of $K_1$.
(*Source:* Stacks Project, Lemma 21.17.12,
[Tag `06YT`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06YT),
and Definition 21.17.13,
[Tag `06YU`](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06YU).)

proof.text: Work on the ringed site $(T_{\Et},\Lambda_T)$ with the direct-sum total tensor and K-flatness of [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Write $\alpha:P\to Q$ for the given quasi-isomorphism and $C=\operatorname{Cone}(\alpha)$. The cone criterion [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] makes $C$ acyclic. The cone clause of [lem-pc-kflat-cone-direct-sum] makes $C$ K-flat, since both $P$ and $Q$ are K-flat. No boundedness or termwise flatness is used.

Apply [lem-pur-acyclic-kflat-tensor-arbitrary] to $C$ and the arbitrary complex $F$. Thus $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes C)$ is acyclic. By [lem-pc-tensor-mapping-cone-iso] it is isomorphic to the cone of $1_F\otimes\alpha$. Apply the converse direction of [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic] to conclude that $1_F\otimes\alpha$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The sign symmetry in [def-kun-derived-tensor] conjugates this map to $\alpha\otimes1_F$, so tensoring on either side has the same property.

Fix a complex $F$ representing $K_2$. Work in the homotopy category of $\Lambda_T$-module complexes. Quasi-isomorphisms have a right calculus of fractions by [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system]. For a derived morphism between K-flat complexes $P,P^{\prime}$, [lem-pc-right-fraction-representation] gives a roof $P\xleftarrow{s}M\xrightarrow{a}P^{\prime}$. Resolve $M$ by $r:R\to M$ using [lem-kun-flat-resolution-existence], so the same roof has K-flat middle $R$ and left leg $sr$. Send it to $\mathsf Q(a r\otimes1_F)\mathsf Q(sr\otimes1_F)^{-1}$, where $\mathsf Q$ is the localization of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]; Step 2 ensures the inverse exists. For two roofs giving the same morphism, [lem-pc-right-fraction-common-refinement] gives a common refinement with equal legs in the homotopy category. Resolve its middle once more. Its maps to the two K-flat middle complexes are quasi-isomorphisms: their composites with the left legs are quasi-isomorphisms, so this follows on cohomology by cancelling isomorphisms. Step 2 inverts their tensors; cancellation then makes the two displayed tensor roofs equal. Tensor respects the homotopies used here: for a degree -1 homotopy $h$ in the first factor, $H(x\otimes y)=h(x)\otimes y$ satisfies $dH+Hd=(dh+hd)\otimes1$, since the two $d_F$ terms have opposite signs. Identities give identity roofs. For composition, take K-flat-middle roofs $P\xleftarrow{s}R\xrightarrow{a}P^{\prime}$ and $P^{\prime}\xleftarrow{t}R^{\prime}\xrightarrow{b}P^{\prime\prime}$. The right-calculus axiom of [lem-pc-quasi-isomorphisms-multiplicative-system] supplies $v:V\to R$ in the quasi-isomorphisms and $w:V\to R^{\prime}$ with $av=tw$. Resolve $V$ by $z:U\to V$ with $U$ K-flat. Put $v_0=vz$ and $w_0=wz$; the composite roof is $(bw_0,sv_0)$. Write $J(f)=\mathsf Q(f\otimes1_F)$. Step 2 makes $J(v_0),J(s),J(t)$ invertible, and $J(a)J(v_0)=J(t)J(w_0)$. Hence $J(bw_0)J(sv_0)^{-1}=J(b)J(w_0)J(v_0)^{-1}J(s)^{-1}=J(b)J(t)^{-1}J(a)J(s)^{-1}$, exactly the composite of the assigned tensor roofs. No invertibility of $w_0$ is required. Thus the rule defines a functor on the full derived subcategory of K-flat representatives, not a choice-dependent map of complexes.

proof.text: Choose two K-flat models $q:P\to C_1$ and $q^{\prime}:P^{\prime}\to C_1$ of a representing complex of $K_1$, as in [def-kun-derived-tensor]. In the derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the specified isomorphism between their images is $u=\mathsf Q(q^{\prime})^{-1}\mathsf Q(q)$. Apply the functor of Step 3 to $u$. It gives the canonical isomorphism $\mathsf Q(P\otimes F)\cong\mathsf Q(P^{\prime}\otimes F)$ between the two prescribed models of $K_1\kunotimes{\Lambda}K_2$. It depends only on $u$, by the refinement argument, and is an isomorphism since a functor sends the inverse of $u$ to its inverse. For a third model, $u_{23}u_{12}=u_{13}$ by cancellation of $\mathsf Q(q_2)$, so functoriality gives the cocycle identity for the comparisons. Every derived object has a K-flat representative by [lem-kun-flat-resolution-existence]; consequently the construction on K-flat representatives defines the same object for any chosen representative of $K_1$, using its specified identification with $K_1$. This is independence up to canonical isomorphism; it does not assert a direct chain map between any two resolutions.

lean.note: Existing declarations for both clauses, specialized to Λ : Type (u + 1), [CommRing Λ], T : Scheme.{u}, A = Sheaf T.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} Λ). For preservation take C = CochainComplex A ℤ and W = HomologicalComplex.quasiIso A (.up ℤ); X ◁ g is the signed direct-sum total tensor map id_X tensor g. Two-out-of-three and K-flat left resolutions are instances from the imports of Etale.Derived.Tensor, not additional mathematical hypotheses. K-flatness agrees with the acyclic-test definition by HomotopyCategory.kFlat_quotient_obj_iff and kFlat_iff_preserves_acyclic, using signed symmetry. For independence take C = HomotopyCategory A (.up ℤ), W = HomotopyCategory.quasiIso A (.up ℤ), L = DerivedCategory.Qh. The recorded isIso_counit_app_app_of_kFlat_left gives the canonical invertible comparison L(P) tensor-derived L(F) → L(P tensor F), natural in both variables. For two models with specified identification u : L(P) ≅ L(P'), the comparison is δ(P,F).symm ≪≫ whiskerRightIso u (L.obj F) ≪≫ δ(P',F). It depends only on u and satisfies identity and cocycle laws by functoriality and cancellation. This is the derived tensor already recorded by def-kun-derived-tensor, in exactly the coefficient category recorded by def-weil-pbc-derived-categories. No new definition, statement correction, module, or stronger flatness/boundedness hypothesis is needed.
